key_insight: Online learning and equilibrium computation are possible even when the learner receives only ordinal (ranking) feedback rather than numeric rewards; the paper designs algorithms that convert rankings into usable signals and prove provable sublinear regret and game-convergence guarantees.
problem_solved: Addresses learning and equilibrium computation when numeric utility signals are unavailable or undesirable (e.g., human-in-the-loop settings or privacy constraints) and only rankings or ordinal comparisons are observed.
method: Formalize an online learning model where the learner observes only rankings/ordinal feedback over actions (possibly partial or adversarial).
Design ordinal-aware online algorithms that aggregate pairwise/comparative information and adapt standard online updates (e.g., FTRL/OMD-style principles) to operate on ranking signals.

Provide theoretical analysis: prove regret bounds for the ordinal algorithms and show that repeated play under ranking feedback converges to game-theoretic equilibria (enabling equilibrium computation without numeric utilities).
impact: Enables robust online decision-making and multi-agent equilibrium computation in settings with human preferences or privacy limits on numeric rewards, broadening applicability of online learning to real-world, ordinal-only feedback scenarios.
visual_elements: Schematic pipeline: environment → ranking-only feedback → ordinal learning algorithm → action/update → (loop), highlighting no numeric rewards.
Comparison chart: numeric-feedback algorithms vs ranking-feedback algorithms (requirements, guarantees, typical applications).
Regret-over-time plot showing sublinear regret (log/log-linear decay) for the proposed ordinal algorithm versus baseline.
Illustration of multi-agent repeated game converging to an equilibrium under ranking feedback (trajectory of strategy profiles).
paper_title: Online Learning and Equilibrium Computation with Ranking Feedback
paper_authors: Mingyang Liu, Yongshan Chen, Zhiyuan Fan, Gabriele Farina, Asuman Ozdaglar
